newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES-JUNE 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES-JUNE 2.

text.p: The following stories were reported in this week's Bulgarian business weeklies. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

-- The Sofia City Court is expected to rule on June 3 on an insolvency suit filed against Slavyani bank by the central bank. The case against the commercial bank, in receivership since September 1996, was postponed on May 12.

-- Bulgaria's parliament dismissed on May 30 the State Savings Bank chairman Bistra Dimitrova for damaging the stability of the country's largest savings institution and appointed as her successor Spas Dimitrov, a lawyer and former deputy of the ruling Union of Democratic Forces.
The National Security Service launched an investigation of SSB earlier this week after receiving signals of illegally transfered funds from the SSB to several private commercial banks.

-- The Sofia City Court is expected to rule on an insolvency suit against private Business Bank on September 30. The bank was put in receivership in September 1996 and a month later the central bank filed an insolvency suit against it in the court.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank must immediately revoke the banking licences of commercial banks against which it has launched bankruptcy procedures, said a report by the International Monetary Fund technical mission which visited the country in the beginning of May.

-- Bulgaria Insurance Holding, one of the country's biggest insurance groupings, bought the ailing private Yambol bank, in receivership since September, for 3.8 billion levs. The ammount, which has been transferred to the central bank accounts, would be used to raise the bank's capital and to cover the bank's debts.
-- Bulgaria will restructure its central bank in line with IMF requirements for introduction of a restrictive fixed exchange rate regime, known as a currency board.
